page: UpCloud GPU-24xCPU-240GB-1xB200 is an x86_64 architecture server powered by an Intel Xeon 8570 processor running at 2.0 GHz. The configuration provides 24 physical cores and 24 vCPUs under a KVM hypervisor, utilizing a shared CPU allocation model. System memory totals 240.0 GB, yielding a resource density of 10.0 GB of RAM per core. A key hardware feature is the integration of a single NVIDIA Blackwell B200 GPU equipped with 192 GB of VRAM. This server does not include local storage.

Benchmark data indicates strong performance in memory bandwidth and data decompression. Read-only small block memory bandwidth reached 4156.98 GB/sec, while large block uncached read and write bandwidths were recorded at 251.17 GB/sec and 115.78 GB/sec respectively. The system achieved a PassMark CPU score of 52754.5 and a database operations score of 25903.08. In LLM inference testing using a small 135M model, the server demonstrated top-tier performance, processing 9953.26 tokens/sec for prompts and generating 525.92 tokens/sec. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reached 352.97 GB/sec, and static web serving throughput was measured at 44.4 GB/sec.

The qualitative cost profile of this server is defined by its high-density GPU and memory resources relative to its shared CPU allocation. While the shared CPU model presents a potential tradeoff for workloads requiring sustained, exclusive CPU cores, the inclusion of the Blackwell B200 GPU with 192 GB VRAM offsets this for parallel computing tasks. The lack of local storage requires external storage integration. This hardware profile is suited for large language model inference, parallel data processing, memory-intensive computations, and GPU-accelerated workloads.
